newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch NMB-Heller buys U.K. company.
newsitem.headline: Dutch NMB-Heller buys U.K. company.

text.p: NMB-Heller Holding NV, a 50-50 joint venture of Fuji Bank Ltd unit Heller International and ING Bank, said on Wednesday it had bought British factoring company TI-Heller Ltd for an undisclosed sum.
NMB-Heller said it saw a further increase in turnover and profits in the current year, excluding the new purchase.
The name of TI-Heller, the biggest independent factoring business in Britain, has been changed to ING-Heller Ltd.
NMB-Heller currently operates in the Netherlands, Germany, Britain, and France and it has started joint ventures in Poland and the Czech Republic.
Turnover of the group would increase by about five billion guilders to 25 billion guilders due to the purchase.
NMB-Heller, a provider of financial services to the international business market, was established in 1967. The key activity of the group is factoring.
"We also have knowledge of financing acquisitions, buy-outs and refinancing plans," director Hans Groenen said.
In 1995, NMB-Heller's turnover was 16.5 billion guilders. Net profits were over 50 million guilders.
